headline: Tech's Earnings Surge Sets the Stage as Geopolitical Fog Hangs Over Friday's Open
body_html:
Futures are pointing to a cautious open on Friday after Thursday's session delivered a split verdict: technology and cybersecurity names surged on blowout earnings, while consumer and homebuilding stocks retreated sharply. Of the 549 names in our universe, 294 finished lower against 252 advancers, underlining a market that is rotating hard rather than rising broadly. Software led all sectors with a gain of roughly 3%, while Homebuilders fell nearly 1.74% to sit at the bottom of the sector table.

The geopolitical backdrop remains the session's sharpest wildcard. Oil is on track for a weekly loss even as the Iran conflict shows no sign of resolution — a top Iranian security official has now attached conditions to any reopening of the Strait of Hormuz, keeping energy traders on edge. A U.S.-hosted G20 finance gathering is expected to address global imbalances and Iran sanctions, while President Trump is said to be convening talks with refiners and fuel retailers as rising gasoline prices loom over the midterm calendar.

Investors will be watching Federal Reserve Governor Warsh's scheduled remarks closely; prediction markets are actively pricing the tone and market impact of his commentary. Apple's forthcoming September product event is also moving into view, offering a potential near-term catalyst for hardware and services sentiment heading into the weekend.

briefs.headline: Okta and Salesforce Earnings Reshape the Software Landscape
briefs.body: Identity-security firm Okta surged 28.63% on Thursday — the biggest single-session move in our universe — while Salesforce climbed 22.58% after its quarterly results challenged bearish narratives around enterprise software demand. The paired gains powered Software to the top sector slot with a 3% advance, lifting sentiment across cloud-adjacent names heading into Friday.

briefs.headline: Cybersecurity Names Post Back-to-Back Standout Sessions
briefs.body: CrowdStrike rose 20.5% and Palo Alto Networks added 12.83% on Thursday, cementing cybersecurity as one of the week's defining themes. The moves arrived alongside strong enterprise-software results, suggesting corporate security budgets remain resilient despite broader macro uncertainty. Both names will be closely tracked at Friday's open for follow-through buying.

briefs.headline: Iran Strait Conditions Rattle Energy Markets Ahead of Weekend
briefs.body: A senior Iranian security official stated publicly that conditions must be met before the Strait of Hormuz could reopen, injecting fresh uncertainty into crude supply routes. Oil is nonetheless headed for a weekly decline, reflecting demand skepticism that is outweighing the geopolitical risk premium — a tension traders will continue to monitor through Friday's close.

briefs.headline: Consumer and Retail Stocks Bear the Brunt of Thursday's Selling
briefs.body: Burlington Stores fell 7.64%, Celsius Holdings dropped 6.36%, Tapestry lost 5.38%, and American Eagle Outfitters declined 5.12% in Thursday's session, dragging the Consumer sector down 1.17%. The broad retail and apparel weakness signals that spending-outlook concerns are cutting across both discount and premium segments as the back-to-school season winds down.

briefs.headline: G20 Finance Gathering Puts Iran Sanctions and Global Imbalances in Focus
briefs.body: A U.S.-hosted G20 finance ministers' meeting is expected to center on growth strategies, trade imbalances, and the expanding Iran sanctions architecture, according to a senior Treasury official. The gathering adds a diplomatic layer to an already complex macro backdrop and could shape near-term currency and commodity positioning ahead of the weekend.

briefs.headline: Warsh Remarks Top the Friday Macro Watch List
briefs.body: Prediction markets are actively handicapping both the content and market reaction to scheduled remarks from Fed Governor Warsh on Friday. With rate-path uncertainty still elevated, any signal on the policy outlook carries outsized weight, and traders are expected to remain cautious ahead of his comments rather than pressing directional bets at the open.
